summary: In this story, two classmates who do not normally get along are paired for a group project and must learn to compromise and divide tasks fairly before realizing they actually work well together.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Project Partner Problem” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: to give up part of what you want so that each side can agree
to work together with someone to get something done
to give someone a particular task or group to be part of

challengeTerms.def: to work together with someone else to produce or achieve something
a particular way of viewing or thinking about a situation
to go well with something else and make it better as a result

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that students should always be allowed to choose their own project partners instead of being assigned one? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Layla and Yousef's different working styles ended up helping, rather than hurting, their project.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review compromise, cooperate, and assign, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use collaborate, perspective, and complement in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
